observations.trace: record_movement_event requires before/after velocities, speed limit and elapsed but maps absent displacement and missing before/after distance pairs to zero. Its acceptance counters can then treat these missing facts like no measured movement. On the selected ordinary producer, record_movement fills actor, distances, displacement, elapsed and speed; BattleRecorder changes sequence and stores the event, resolve_battle returns that timeline. Terminal events intentionally lack an actor and are skipped.
observations.remaining: This is the existing Adler059 finding, with source counterevidence for the ordinary route; public event fields, alternate callers, per-kind policy and exact aliases remain open. No malformed event or report ran.

observations.trace: The selected duel constructs distinct left/right Entities with Party/Enemy sides and Player names. Resolved contact retains attacker/target Entities and typed anatomy, but logging copies names into String event fields. Private causal accounting routes a name matching John to John and any other name to the opponent; victory records a name and runner separately rejects a name matching neither roster name.
observations.remaining: The two original Segovb findings remain distinct: their first conversion and consumers differ. The fixed roster is not shown to contain duplicate names or unknown actors; human text remains legitimate native presentation. Autoresolve numeric IDs have a separate namespace.

observations.trace: MeleeAttackResolved carries AnatomicalSubregion; resolved_attack_entry passes it through a generic serde_json value and as_str expects into a String event, then the private report increments a String-keyed anatomical map. The selected enum has twelve unit cases with snake_case Serde. Autoresolve independently formats its typed four-case MeleeContactClassification with Debug before its private String map.
observations.remaining: Same original Segovb findings, not new historic discoveries or aliases. No serializer or invalid value ran, no ordinary panic claimed. Final output key policy and full upstream coverage remain open.

observations.trace: The command rejects either zero seed count before creating the output directory; the source roster returns five opponents. It writes acceptance evidence before matchup runs, and returns a batch error before writing its summary, while earlier trace output or other existing files may remain. Report measurements reject nonfinite contact-energy input, but the partition check directly sums separate f32 components and compares absolute error.
observations.remaining: No filesystem or CLI execution; exact NaN reachability or false acceptance is not established. The all-weapon band set and label question is separately recorded; all false boolean gating and native consumers require policy evidence.

observations.trace: Tactical ArmorLayerContact retains catalogue item_id:String, optional inventory_item_id and typed material; its causal report formats catalogue item and Debug material as a combined String key. Autoresolve ArmorLayerTelemetry instead retains optional numeric inventory_item_id and optional material and formats those as its own key.
observations.remaining: These namespaces and possible absence differ; no automatic alias, collision or blanket mandatory inventory identity is inferred. Native key serialization and canonical item identity policy remain open.

conditional_findings.first_contract: The report owner must make the scope of its all-weapon contact-band assertion explicit and ensure the named evidence set covers the intended weapon population.
conditional_findings.source_witness: The fixed melee iteration roster passes five distinct weapon IDs into its builds: longsword, arming_sword, halberd, war_hammer and baselard. melee_iteration_acceptance_evidence selects only John, hammer and veteran for all_weapon_contact_band_evidence, which emits five band samples per selected build with separately hard-coded longsword, war_hammer and halberd labels. The audit field all_weapon_swept_contact_contract_holds checks those samples and separate per-matchup summary conditions. There is no explicit arming_sword or baselard band generated by this helper.
conditional_findings.counterevidence: Other tactical/autoresolve batch summaries are checked per matchup, and the three bands may be intentionally representative rather than a promise for every roster weapon. Source inspection does not establish that the acceptance boolean becomes true, that a missing sample would fail, or that any report or incident exists.
conditional_findings.effect_and_limits: Conditional evidence-scope and naming question. If all roster weapons are intended, these explicit band samples do not cover two selected weapon IDs; if representative classes are intended, the precise contract and labels need an owning decision. Catalog-wide coverage is not inferred from the finite roster.
conditional_findings.repair_direction: When authorized, reconcile the intended population with the report owner; derive checked cases and labels from actual weapon owners for exhaustive coverage, or explicitly name and document a representative sample if that is the policy. Preserve per-matchup checks and distinct native presentation.
conditional_findings.alias_qualification: Recovered pending questions ask for actual producer, roster and evidence coverage; this bounded current observation does not establish a global alias, historical unique-count change or checkpoint3821 authority.
